title: Wave Process Summary: Functionality

children:
A wave represents the different steps that the system uses to retrieve orders from the pool, and process 
 them into the outbound portion of SCALE.  All wave activity is defined on the wave master 
 record. The system uses this master record to identify how to execute the wave during the run wave process, and what entities to create from the shipments included in the wave (such as allocation requests, containers, etc).
Container Creation in the Wave Process Summary
The following are key features of the wave functional area:

The wave priority value determines when the wave is initiated, in relation 
 to other wave records. The lower the priority number, the sooner the wave 
 is run.

The wave criteria determines which shipments will be processed by a 
 wave. You can set the wave criteria on any combination of shipment 
 values. This allows you to create wave records for particular customers, 
 carriers, or other shipment specific value.
A wave mode determines how a wave is initiated.

Automatic - When you process 
 a wave in automatic mode, the system will automatically run it after the 
 build wave process is complete. This provides a streamlined approach and 
 minimizes user intervention.

Build Inactive - The wave 
 is not available for use at this time. The system will not run this wave. 
 This mode allows you turn off a wave that you don't want to delete, but 
 should not currently use. Build Inactive is commonly used for seasonal 
 items.

Manual - When you process 
 a wave in manual mode, you must manually select to run a wave. The system 
 will not automatically run it for you. Manual build is helpful for large 
 waves. It also allows you to manage processing time demands per wave.

Scheduled - When you process 
 a wave in scheduled mode, the system will run this wave according to the 
 time interval defined on the Scheduled Job Window.

A wave maximum determines how many shipments can be included in a wave. 
 Any combination of the following values can be used to define a wave maximum:
Total number of units (defined at the container type level)

Wave Process Summary
        ** Functionality **
        
        Process Flows
        
         
         
        Summary...
        A wave represents the different steps that the system uses to retrieve orders from the pool, and process 
 them into the outbound portion of SCALE.  All wave activity is defined on the wave master 
 record. The system uses this master record to identify how to execute the wave during the run wave process, and what entities to create from the shipments included in the wave (such as allocation requests, containers, etc). 
         
         
         
        Related Topics...
        - Setup Overviews
        - Container Creation in the Wave Process Summary
        - Creating a New Wave
        - Processing a Wave
         
         
         
        The following are key features of the wave functional area:
         
         
        Wave Priority...
        The wave priority value determines when the wave is initiated, in relation 
 to other wave records. The lower the priority number, the sooner the wave 
 is run.
         
         
         
        Wave Criteria...
        The wave criteria determines which shipments will be processed by a 
 wave. You can set the wave criteria on any combination of shipment 
 values. This allows you to create wave records for particular customers, 
 carriers, or other shipment specific value.
         
         
         
        Wave Modes...
        A wave mode determines how a wave is initiated.
        
            
                Automatic - When you process 
 a wave in automatic mode, the system will automatically run it after the 
 build wave process is complete. This provides a streamlined approach and 
 minimizes user intervention.
                 
            
            
                Build Inactive - The wave 
 is not available for use at this time. The system will not run this wave. 
 This mode allows you turn off a wave that you don't want to delete, but 
 should not currently use. Build Inactive is commonly used for seasonal 
 items.
                 
            
            
                Manual - When you process 
 a wave in manual mode, you must manually select to run a wave. The system 
 will not automatically run it for you. Manual build is helpful for large 
 waves. It also allows you to manage processing time demands per wave.
                 
            
            
                Scheduled - When you process 
 a wave in scheduled mode, the system will run this wave according to the 
 time interval defined on the Scheduled Job Window.
            
        
         
         
        Wave Maximums...
        A wave maximum determines how many shipments can be included in a wave. 
 Any combination of the following values can be used to define a wave maximum:
        
            
                Total number of shipments
                 
            
            
                Total number of shipment details
                 
            
            
                Total number of units (defined at the container type level)
                 
            
            
                Maximum value of product
                 
            
            
                Maximum weight of product
                 
            
            Maximum volume of product
